research_question: What is the effect of intranasal steroids compared with no steroid treatment on persistence of otitis media with effusion in children at up to 1 month?
control_label: No steroid treatment (no treatment or identical co-treatment alone)
outcome_description: Persistence of middle ear effusion at the first assessment up to 1 month after treatment initiation (dichotomous outcome)
positive_direction: Favors intranasal steroids (lower rate of persistent otitis media with effusion)
search_queries: intranasal steroids otitis media effusion children trial
topical steroid spray persistent middle ear effusion controlled study
intranasal corticosteroid glue ear comparison quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Children diagnosed with otitis media with effusion (OME or glue ear)
Comparison of intranasal corticosteroids (with or without co-treatment) against no steroid treatment (no treatment or identical co-treatment alone)
Quantitative reporting of persistent middle ear effusion or resolution at follow-up up to 1 month
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, commentaries, editorials, and case reports are excluded)
No comparison between intranasal steroids and a no-steroid control (studies evaluating oral steroids or using a placebo control are excluded)
No quantitative outcome data on middle ear effusion persistence or resolution up to 1 month that can produce an effect size
Completely unrelated to otitis media with effusion in children
moderators_to_extract: Specific intranasal corticosteroid agent and daily dose
Follow-up duration within the 1-month window (e.g., 2 weeks vs 4 weeks)
Type of concurrent co-treatment administered to both groups (e.g., antibiotics, antihistamines, none)
effect_size_note: Dichotomous outcome measured as persistence of effusion at up to 1 month; positive effect sizes indicate reduction in persistent effusion favoring intranasal steroids.
single_outcome_target: persistence of otitis media with effusion
